newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil recuperates on futures and premiums.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil recuperates on futures and premiums.

text.p: NWE gas oil was slightly stronger on Wednesday as benchmark IPE futures recuperated from Tuesday's fall and premiums firmed slightly, traders said.
June IPE gas oil was trading 75 cents higher at $172.75 a tonne at 1142 GMT, having shed some $5.75 on Tuesday.
Traders said the substantial outright price fall on the back of futures on Tuesday had failed to entice buyers back into the market.
"There were quite a few enquiries in early on, but then it just fizzled out," one trader said.
A 1,000 tonne heating oil barge traded at June IPE +$1.75 fob Rotterdam for first half June early on, but otherwise traders said it was very quiet.
Heating oil barge premiums were assessed at June IPE +$1.50/+$2.50 fob Rotterdam for prompt delivery and 50 cents below there for first half June delivery.
Diesel premiums were also slightly firmer with offers seen around June IPE +$10.
There was little action the cargo front, although traders said there was a fair amount of Russian material on offer at around June IPE +$2.50 cif NWE.
